title: What well control and production safety training does BSEE require offshore, and is Subpart O still in force?
seoTitle: BSEE well control training: Subpart O
description: BSEE well control, deepwater well control and production safety training under 30 CFR 250 Subpart O, weekly drills and BSEE testing, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Yes. As at November 2026, 30 CFR 250 Subpart O, "Well Control and Production Safety Training", remains in force alongside the SEMS rule. It requires Outer Continental Shelf lessees to train employees to competently perform well control, deepwater well control and production safety duties, to keep a written training plan, verify contractors' training, and to produce 5 years of training records on request. Separately, 30 CFR 250.711 requires a weekly well control drill for everyone engaged in well operations.
keyTakeaways: Subpart O (sections 250.1500 to 250.1510) is current in the eCFR, so well control and production safety training is a stand-alone duty, not only a SEMS element.
Anyone working with a subsea blowout preventer stack must be trained in deepwater well control and have comprehensive knowledge of its equipment, practices and theory (250.1503(b)).
The training plan must specify the type, method, length, frequency and content of training and how understanding and performance are verified (250.1503(c)).
The lessee sets training frequency, but must provide periodic training, verify knowledge retention, and ensure contractors do the same (250.1506).
BSEE can audit the training system, interview and test personnel, and require hands-on, simulator or live well testing at the lessee's cost (250.1507 to 250.1509).
regulator: Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE), US Department of the Interior
appliesTo: Lessees engaged in oil, gas or sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf, including BOEM-approved assignees and owners of operating rights
Lessee employees assigned well control, deepwater well control or production safety duties

sections.heading: Is 30 CFR 250 Subpart O still current?

blocks.text: Yes. The eCFR structure for 30 CFR part 250, checked in November 2026, lists Subpart O, "Well Control and Production Safety Training", with sections 250.1500, 250.1501 and 250.1503 to 250.1510, separate from Subpart S, "Safety and Environmental Management Systems (SEMS)". Section [250.1500](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1500) carries amendment notes from October 18, 2011 and August 22, 2012.

The two subparts work at different levels. Subpart S requires a management system in which all personnel are trained for their duties, as described in [BSEE SEMS offshore training requirements](/regulations/bsee-sems-offshore-training-requirements). Subpart O imposes specific duties for the people who control wells and run production safety systems, including a written training plan and BSEE testing powers. An operator needs to satisfy both.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: A BSEE rule published June 10, 2026 and effective August 10, 2026 updated documents incorporated by reference across part 250. It did not amend the Subpart O training sections. Check the eCFR before relying on this page after November 2026.

sections.heading: Which duties and people does Subpart O cover?

blocks.text: Section 250.1500 defines the three duty areas. **Well control** means methods to minimize the potential for the well to flow or kick and to maintain control if it does, across drilling, completion, workover, abandonment and well-servicing, including fluid flow monitoring and the installation, repair, maintenance and operation of surface and subsea well control equipment. **Deepwater well control** means well control when using a subsea blowout preventer (BOP) system. **Production safety** covers measures, practices, procedures and equipment for safe, accident-free and pollution-free production, including surface and subsurface safety equipment.

The definitions also settle two points that affect scope. Employees are the lessee's direct employees assigned those duties, and contractors are anyone other than an employee performing them for the lessee. "Periodic" means occurring at regular intervals, and each lessee must specify the intervals for periodic training and for periodic assessment of training needs in its own program.

Under section [250.1501](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1501), the goal of the training program must be safe and clean OCS operations, achieved by ensuring that employees and contract personnel engaged in these operations understand and can properly perform their duties.

sections.heading: What must the Subpart O training plan contain?

blocks.text: Section [250.1503](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1503) requires the lessee to establish and implement a training program so that all employees are trained to competently perform their assigned duties, and to verify that employees understand and can perform them. The written plan must specify the type, method or methods, length, frequency and content of training, and the methods of verifying understanding and performance. At a minimum it must include:

items: Procedures for training employees in well control, deepwater well control or production safety practices.
Procedures for evaluating the training programs of contractors.
Procedures for verifying that all employees and contractor personnel engaged in these operations can perform their assigned duties.
Procedures for assessing the training needs of employees on a periodic basis.

blocks.text: On request of the District Manager or Regional Supervisor, the lessee must provide copies of training documentation for personnel involved in these operations during the past 5 years, and a copy of the training plan. A five-year record set per person is therefore the practical minimum.

sections.heading: How flexible are training methods and frequency?

blocks.text: Methods are flexible but must be reinforced. Section 250.1504 allows alternative methods such as computer-based learning, films or equivalents, which "should be reinforced by appropriate demonstrations and 'hands-on' training" and must meet the training plan's objectives. Section 250.1505 lets lessees obtain training from any source that meets the plan.

Frequency is set by the lessee, within limits. Under section [250.1506](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1506), the lessee must provide periodic training to maintain understanding of, and competency in, the relevant practices; establish procedures to verify adequate retention of the knowledge and skills employees need; and ensure that contractors' training programs provide periodic training and verification. A [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) step after each training cycle is the most direct way to show retention.

Well control drills reinforce the training. Under [30 CFR 250.711](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.711), the operator must conduct a weekly well control drill with all personnel engaged in well operations, to familiarize them with their roles under the well control plan. Drills must cover a range of operations, including drilling with a diverter, on-bottom drilling and tripping, and the same drill may not be repeated consecutively with the same crew. Each drill's date, time, type, time to be ready to close the diverter or use each BOP component, and total time must be recorded in the daily report.

sections.heading: How does BSEE test training results?

blocks.text: BSEE can go beyond paperwork. Under section [250.1507](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-30/section-250.1507), BSEE or its authorized representative may conduct a training system audit at the lessee's office, interview employees and contract personnel onshore or offshore about the training they received and how effective it was, test individuals' knowledge and skills, and run hands-on production safety, simulator or live well tests. The lessee pays the costs of testing, excluding BSEE salary and travel.

When BSEE tests, sections 250.1508 and 250.1509 require the lessee and its contractors to allow the testing and to identify each person by current position, years in that position, total years of oilfield experience and employer. A BSEE representative may also order a well control drill during an inspection under section 250.711(c), after consulting the onsite representative.

If the training program does not comply, section 250.1510 allows BSEE to issue an Incident of Noncompliance, require a revised training plan, assess civil or criminal penalties, or initiate disqualification procedures.

blocks.text: Because contractors fall under both Subpart O and SEMS, the guide on [training contractors and temporary workers](/guides/how-to-train-contractors-and-temporary-workers) is a useful companion for drilling and service company crews.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures well control and production safety competences as assessment points per role and BOP configuration, linked to the drills and tests that verify them. That makes the Subpart O training plan, the five-year record set and the SEMS training element one connected body of evidence rather than three separate files. More on how this applies across the sector is on the [energy and resources](/industries/energy-resources) page.

faqs.q: Did SEMS replace Subpart O training requirements?
faqs.a: No. As at November 2026 the eCFR lists Subpart O, sections 250.1500 to 250.1510, as current alongside Subpart S. Subpart S covers training for all personnel within the management system, while Subpart O sets specific requirements for well control, deepwater well control and production safety duties.

faqs.q: How often must offshore well control training be repeated under BSEE rules?
faqs.a: Subpart O does not fix an interval. Section 250.1506 lets the lessee determine the frequency but requires periodic training, procedures to verify knowledge retention, and assurance that contractors do the same. The interval must be written into the training plan.

faqs.q: Can well control training be delivered online?
faqs.a: Partly. Section 250.1504 allows computer-based learning, films or equivalents, but says the training should be reinforced by appropriate demonstrations and hands-on training and must meet the objectives of the training plan. BSEE can also require hands-on or simulator testing.

faqs.q: Who pays when BSEE tests offshore personnel?
faqs.a: The lessee. Sections 250.1507 and 250.1509 make the lessee responsible for the costs of hands-on, simulator or other testing that BSEE conducts or requires, excluding salary and travel costs for BSEE personnel.
